hero.title: Welcome to My Portfolio
hero.subtitle: Full Stack Developer
hero.intro: Hi, my name is José. I'm a Full Stack developer currently working for myself. I build web and mobile solutions for clients, from static sites to complex platforms and all their infrastructure.

about.title: About Me
about.paragraph1: In 2022 I decided to pursue my passion for programming, which led me to new experiences, meeting colleagues, and learning the current market technologies to develop web and mobile applications. Since then I have stayed on this continuous and ever-changing learning path. My main stack is React and Nest.js for web apps, and React Native for Android and iOS, alongside a modern, agentic AI-powered workspace.
about.paragraph2: When I'm not coding, I enjoy researching new technologies and staying up to date with the latest news. I'm currently learning Bevy: a new game engine written in Rust, and learning to build games in my free time. Please check out the next section 👇.

spaceinvaders.title: Space Invaders Game
spaceinvaders.instructions: Use A and D keys to move and space to shoot
spaceinvaders.subtitle: My first game project
spaceinvaders.description: This tutorial taught me the basics of Bevy, from how to set up a project to using the ECS (Entity Component System), where entities relate to components and game logic is applied. I learned to move the player and enemies, render projectiles, and manage collisions between them. It was an excellent project to start familiarizing myself with Bevy.

platformer.title: Platformer Game
platformer.subtitle: A game promise
platformer.instructions: Use arrow keys to move, SPACE to jump, Z for light attack and V for heavy attack
platformer.description:
After learning the basics with Bevy, I felt the urge to create something more attractive, something that would really make people want to play and allow me to learn how to make a game that excites, like those I played as a child. I started with what I already knew: rendering a sprite on screen and applying what I learned in my first project to move the player, detect collisions, and make it possible to move around a map. At first it was overwhelming to know which path to follow to advance with the game's functionalities, but little by little priorities emerged, such as animating the character using texture atlases, iterating over sprites and displaying them on screen in an animated way.

Later, I incorporated a physics system to simulate gravity and ensure that the map entities behaved as expected. Once that solid foundation was built, I started adding essential functionalities for a basic game: the enemy. Implementing it wasn't too difficult, but I realized that it didn't make much sense to have a player and an enemy if they couldn't attack each other. That's how I integrated a collision, health and damage system, which allowed me to dive much deeper into Bevy and Rust.

There's still a lot to do to achieve an interesting and fun game, but I think that, as a demo, it's a good example of my progress in learning game development.
